_about: What the port's lighting reads that no level file carries. Levels carry their own ambient,
emissive and lightmaps as metadata/eth_* keys (sim/Lighting.hpp); this is what the ORIGINAL'S
SCRIPT sets over them. The remake's out/parity/specs/lighting/design_port.md, section 5.9, and
Only what a built step reads is here: the two ambient lights the script sets (G3, step 45), and
the normal maps' green and the halo scale (G5, step 49), and the 16-bit framebuffer (G6, step 55).
The design's other row - the script emissive overrides - arrives with the step that reads it.

_source: Moved from art.json's darkest block. Game's level-properties reader does
CheckCustomData('darkest') and, when it is set, SetAmbientLight(DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT); that
one call is the whole of what the flag does there. DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT is built at
Game.angelscript bytes 306783..306841 as vector3(0.01, 0.01, 0.01): very nearly black, not
black. It REPLACES the level file's own <Ambient> - level21c (4-22) says 0.5 and draws at
0.01 - and ETHCallback_fire_signal sets it again when a torch is put back out
(torch.json, signal).
Moved from torch.json's ambient.lit. ETHCallback_light_off's `delete` branch, run on the
frame after the torch is shot, calls SetAmbientLight(0.1, 0.1, 0.25) - lighter than
darkest's 0.01, and blue, but not lit - then lightenAllBackgroundEntitities and
GenerateLightmaps (bytes 467198..473086). Those two are the design's step G6, not this.
Decoded, not tested for. The original's light shader, hPixelLightDiff.ps (shaders.h:1261-1304 in
the shipped library; the remake's engine_math.md 4.5), decodes a normal-map texel c as
-(2 (c - 0.5)) and dots it with (P - L) in Ethanon's world, whose y points DOWN the screen. So a
green above one half faces down the image, where the port's world is y-up: the engine flips it
(MaterialComponent::Sprite2DLight::normalYDown). The port's torch pass on the player (step 49)
is the measurement that would show the other sense.
What every <Light><HaloBitmap> halo's formula colour, <Color> x haloBrightness x the owner's live
particle ratio (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:354-388), is multiplied by. Ethanon has no such factor: 1 is
its formula. The design leaves the number to the halo gate (design_port.md 5.5 and 8), and the
gate says one is needed: at 1 the port reads 8.94 of 255 on 1-01's LM_E<1_halo blocks against
the original (asked 6.0), and the remake's fit, drawn with 1x art at the brightness the port drew
(its torch's flame 10 of 12 live at frame 420), reads 8.88 there, so it is the brightness and
not the art. The fit finds x0.5 of the formula's maximum on the arch with the strongest halo
signal in both 1-01 and 1-09 (fit.md 6).
_measured: Step 49, frame 420, the port against the original, LM_E<1_halo on 1-01 / on 1-09 / noLM_E=1_halo
both LM_E<1_halo rows: drawn with 1x art the fit's own model reads at least 5.84 on 1-09 at any
brightness (2.97 with the original's hd art), and above 6 on 1-01 past an effective 0.55.
_note: 0.6 is the value those rows favour: 1-01 passes and 1-09 misses by 0.17, inside the 1x floor. It
is tuned to one frame's flame. Over 20 s the torch's flame is 0.7265 live (test_mp_layer), so
0.6 draws the halo at 0.44 of the formula on average, where 0.69 would match the fit's 0.5 on
average and 1 would be Ethanon's own arithmetic. For the owner, and for plan_port System 6.

_source: The original asks Android for a 5/6/5 surface and draws into it without dithering: GL2JNIView.java:94
and ConfigChooser.java:48-67 in the shipped APK (the remake's engine_math.md 0.2). The remake's fit
of its pixels scores 0.28 of 255 on dark sprites with the 5/6/5 step and 0.62 without (fit.md 9).
The engine quantises the composite (RenderSettings::OutputQuantize::Rgb565); the screen overlay
drawn after it - the HUD, the pause, the menus - is not quantised.
